title: Best Privacy Browsers Compared
metaDescription: Brave, Firefox and Incognito Browser (which we make) compared on ad blocking, tracker and fingerprint protection, and open source code, on one rubric.
intro: Choosing the right privacy browser is one of the most impactful steps for online privacy.

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Runs in private mode all the time; history, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit
Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option
Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, and can load desktop sites
Settings to turn images, JavaScript and cookies on or off
cons: Android only: no iOS, desktop or web version
Does not claim tracker or fingerprint protection
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Brave
pros: Installs Chrome Web Store extensions on desktop

products.name: Firefox
products.tagline: Open-source browser with Enhanced Tracking Protection
cons: Strict tracking protection can break some sites

incognito-browser.note: Built-in ad blocker with a High Security Blocking option

firefox.note: Tracking protection blocks some ad trackers; full ad blocking needs an extension

incognito-browser.note: Automatic tracker blocking is not in the app's verified feature list; cookies are wiped when you exit
Not claimed. Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not fingerprint protection

firefox.note: Blocks known fingerprinting scripts by default; Mozilla's stronger protections are on only in private windows and Strict mode

verdict.summary: On these four criteria Brave scores highest: it blocks ads, trackers and fingerprinting by default and is open source. Firefox is second: it is open source and blocks known trackers by default, but full ad blocking needs an extension. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest here: it has a built-in ad blocker and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit, but it is not open source, does not claim tracker or fingerprint protection, and runs only on Android.

bestFor.reason: Highest score here: ad, tracker and fingerprint blocking are on by default, and its code is open source
The desktop version installs extensions from the Chrome Web Store; Brave on Android does not support extensions
Open source, with add-ons on desktop and Android and advanced settings in about:config on desktop

faqs.question: Can I use Chrome extensions in a privacy browser?
faqs.answer: On desktop, Brave installs extensions from the Chrome Web Store. Firefox has its own add-on store on desktop and Android. Brave on Android does not support extensions, and extensions are not among Incognito Browser's listed features.

faqs.question: Will switching browsers affect my saved passwords?
faqs.answer: On desktop, Brave and Firefox can import bookmarks and saved passwords from Chrome. Incognito Browser keeps no browsing history and does not list a password manager among its features, so if you switch to it, keep your passwords in a separate password manager.
